title: Blood chemistry test
what: A blood test from a vein that shows how your liver, kidneys, and metabolism are working. Your doctor chooses which values to check.
why: For checkups, liver and kidney disease, diabetes, before surgery, and to track treatment.
duration: the blood draw takes 3 to 5 minutes; results usually come in 1 to 2 days
tell_doctor: What medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take
If you recently had hard workouts or an injury

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually strictly fasting: no food for 8 to 12 hours. Plain water is fine. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: Eat a light dinner with no fatty food. For one day before, no alcohol and no hard workouts.

prepare.title: In the morning
prepare.text: Do not smoke. Do not drink tea, coffee, or juice, and do not chew gum.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Ask your doctor whether to take your morning medicines before or after the test.

bring: Your referral with the list of tests
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tied above your elbow
The skin is cleaned with antiseptic
A quick prick, and blood fills the tube
The needle is removed, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes
You can eat right after the test
Your doctor explains the results. One number out of range is not a diagnosis

faq.q: Why must I fast for blood chemistry?
faq.a: Food changes your sugar, fats, and other values. A test after breakfast may show false results.
There is no single set. It usually includes liver tests, creatinine, sugar, protein, and cholesterol. Your doctor decides the list.

reminders.text: Blood chemistry test tomorrow. After a light dinner, do not eat. Water is fine. No alcohol.
